title: Kidney transplant (recipient operation)
subtitle: Extraperitoneal iliac fossa implantation, vascular anastomoses and ureteroneocystostomy

sources.title: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline on the Evaluation and Management of Candidates for Kidney Transplantation
Guidelines for Living Donor Kidney Transplantation, 4th edition
Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 1994 (amended 2011) and Rules 2014

indications: End-stage kidney disease in a patient assessed and listed as suitable for transplantation (pre-emptive where possible).
contraindications: Active infection or malignancy, a positive crossmatch not overcome by a desensitisation protocol, prohibitive cardiovascular risk, or uncontrolled disease that would compromise the graft.
preparation: Confirm ABO compatibility, a negative crossmatch, the HLA and donor information, and the organ's cold ischaemia time.
Dialysis status, potassium and fluid balance; immunosuppression induction plan agreed with nephrology.
Consent: graft failure and rejection, bleeding, thrombosis, urine leak, lymphocele, infection, and the risks carried from the donor.
positioning: Supine, a urinary catheter with a three-way connection to fill the bladder, arms out, the fistula arm protected and labelled.
equipment: Vascular set, bulldog and vascular clamps, 5-0 and 6-0 non-absorbable vascular sutures, an ice bowl for the kidney, ureteric stent, urine catheter set-up for bladder filling, Doppler probe.
anatomy: The right iliac fossa (often preferred): external iliac artery and vein, the lymphatics over them, the bladder, the inferior epigastric vessels, the spermatic cord or round ligament.
The graft: renal artery (often on a Carrel patch of donor aorta), renal vein, ureter with its blood supply in the periureteric tissue.
criticalSafety: Check ABO, crossmatch and the donor organ details aloud before the kidney is opened from its packaging.
Keep the kidney cold until reperfusion, and record warm and cold ischaemia times.
Avoid kinking or twisting the vessels when placing the kidney.
structuresAtRisk: Femoral nerve and lateral cutaneous nerve of thigh (retractor injury)
complications: Bleeding, lymphocele, urine leak or ureteric stenosis.
postop: Fluid and blood pressure targets agreed for graft perfusion; hourly urine output.
Doppler ultrasound of the graft early (often day 0 or 1) and urgently for any fall in urine output.
Immunosuppression and prophylaxis per protocol; stent removal date recorded.

steps.emphasis: Includes the donor-derived risks and the immunosuppression commitment.
Read recipient and donor ABO, the crossmatch result, organ side and cold ischaemia time aloud.
Antibiotic prophylaxis and the induction immunosuppression timed per the transplant protocol.
Supine, catheter connected for bladder filling, fistula arm protected and labelled.
Clamp the external iliac vein and artery only when the kidney is ready on ice.
Renal artery (Carrel patch) to the external iliac artery, end to side.
Warn the anaesthetist; the blood pressure target is high enough to perfuse the graft. Record the time of reperfusion.
The kidney turns pink and firm uniformly; watch for urine from the ureter.
A double-J stent across the ureteroneocystostomy; record it for removal.
Check the hilum and the anastomoses; immunosuppressed patients bleed late.
A drain near the graft, away from the anastomoses.
Hand over ischaemia times, the anastomoses, the stent, the fluid and blood pressure plan, and when to scan the graft.

step.tx.organ-check.title: Donor organ and compatibility check
step.tx.organ-check.why: Transplanting into the wrong recipient, or across an incompatible blood group, can cause hyperacute rejection. The checks happen before the kidney leaves its packaging.
how: Confirm recipient identity, ABO compatibility of donor and recipient, a negative crossmatch and the donor information.
Confirm the organ (side, anatomy, number of arteries) against the offer paperwork; note the cold ischaemia time.
In India, confirm the authorisation documentation required under the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act for living donor cases.
pitfalls: Opening the organ before the checks.

step.tx.bench.title: Bench preparation of the kidney
step.tx.bench.why: Preparing the kidney on ice prevents warm injury and shows the vessels and ureter so the anastomoses are planned before the clamps go on.
how: Keep the kidney in a bowl of ice slush throughout.
Trim excess perirenal fat, tie lymphatics and small vessels at the hilum, and identify the artery (with its Carrel patch), the vein and the ureter.
Preserve the tissue between the lower pole and the ureter (the golden triangle) which carries the ureteric blood supply.
Repair or reconstruct multiple arteries or short veins as needed.

step.tx.exposure.title: Extraperitoneal exposure of the iliac vessels
step.tx.exposure.why: The iliac fossa gives a retroperitoneal bed close to the bladder. Lymphatics over the vessels are tied rather than cut to prevent a lymphocele.
how: Make a curvilinear (Rutherford Morison) incision in the iliac fossa; divide the muscles and push the peritoneum medially.
Divide or preserve the inferior epigastric vessels and the round ligament or protect the spermatic cord.
Expose the external iliac artery and vein, tying the overlying lymphatics.
structuresAtRisk: Femoral and lateral cutaneous nerves (retractor blades)
pitfalls: A self-retaining retractor blade on the psoas compressing the femoral nerve.

step.tx.venous.title: Renal vein to external iliac vein anastomosis
step.tx.venous.why: The venous anastomosis is usually done first. A narrowed or twisted vein causes graft thrombosis within hours.
how: Clamp the external iliac vein, make a venotomy matched to the renal vein, and sew end to side with a fine non-absorbable continuous suture.
Orient the kidney before suturing so the vein does not twist when the graft is placed.

step.tx.poor-perfusion.title: Bailout: a graft that does not perfuse
step.tx.poor-perfusion.why: Patchy, soft or dusky perfusion after reperfusion means a technical problem until proven otherwise, and it is reversible only while the patient is still on the table.
how: Check the blood pressure with the anaesthetist and the position of the kidney for kinks or twists.
Feel and Doppler the artery and vein; look for a dissection flap or thrombosis.
Redo the anastomosis if needed, flushing the kidney cold again; involve a senior transplant surgeon early.
Record the findings; a non-perfusing kidney may have to be removed.
pitfalls: Closing over a poorly perfused graft and hoping.

step.tx.ureter.title: Ureteroneocystostomy
step.tx.ureter.why: A short, well-vascularised ureter joined to the bladder with an anti-reflux tunnel (Lich-Gregoir) gives the fewest leaks and stenoses.
how: Fill the bladder through the catheter and expose its dome or side.
Shorten the ureter to a length that lies without tension, keeping its blood supply.
Open the detrusor down to mucosa, anastomose ureteric mucosa to bladder mucosa over a stent, and close the detrusor over it as a tunnel.
